R337 — phase cache VMM and two-GEN lifetime audit
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Status: SOURCE ONLY / UNVERIFIED. Read-only audit of packet `main-phase-decode-cache-serve-source-v3` against its contract, plan, R322/R333, production source baseline, and primary SYCL/Level Zero documentation. No packet/worktree/source/receipt mutation, build, test, import, GPU/model/process/service operation, Git mutation, or cleanup. This report is the only new artifact.

## Result

One concrete conditional VMM correctness gap remains: the owner uses device physical-memory granularity to size its virtual reservation, but does not query the distinct context reservation granularity. If the computed reservation size is not a multiple of the context's minimum granularity, `reserve_virtual_mem` has undefined behavior under the SYCL extension. The packet's additional 2-MiB LCM does not establish divisibility by an independently larger or otherwise incompatible context granularity. Whether the qualified single-device B570 runtime has this mismatch is unmeasured, so this is a source guard omission, not a claim that that target necessarily fails.

The source does correctly keep extents within stable reserved virtual addresses, maintain 144 initial plus per-layer extra slot membership, block reads from unbacked/unverified slots, drain before transitions, and retain uncertain native owners after failures. I found no further concrete two-GEN alias/lifetime defect in the admitted mode by static inspection. This does not qualify compilation, driver behavior, producer completion, or actual two-GEN runtime safety.

## Finding and evidence

In the packet, `after/src/core/gpu.cpp:166-168` implements `vmem_granularity()` as `get_mem_granularity(rt().device(), rt().context(), granularity_mode::recommended)`: this is the device granularity query. `after/src/core/phase_cache_backend.cpp:18-20` reports that value in `Caps.granularity`, and `after/src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp:22-28,44-53,69-102` applies its LCM with 2 MiB to physical and virtual extent sizes before calling reserve. No context-only granularity is queried.

Intel's primary SYCL extension states that device granularity governs physical allocations while context granularity governs virtual reservations; the context overload can return a separate value. It requires reservation sizes to be multiples of the context's minimum granularity, and explicitly says violating that requirement is undefined behavior. The physical-memory mapping separately requires physical-device minimum granularity. See [Intel SYCL virtual memory extension, granularity and reserve rules](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_virtual_mem.asciidoc#memory-granularity) and [the same extension, physical-memory and mapping requirements](https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_virtual_mem.asciidoc#physical-memory-representation).

Concrete condition and consequence: if `alignment(device_recommended, 2 MiB)` does not divide evenly by `context_minimum`, then at least one computed `reserved_` total may be invalid for `reserve_virtual_mem`; the current code still submits it. The extension specifies undefined behavior for an invalid reservation size. A conforming implementation may throw, but correctness cannot rely on that. The safe source guard is to query both granularities, validate each extent's allocation/map constraints against the device minimum, and round/validate the total reservation against the context minimum before any native ownership. The current B570 + sourceLLVM7.1.1/URv2 actual values must be recorded by Main; no values were queried in this audit.

## Two-GEN lifetime / alias review

- Owner geometry in `phase_cache_owner.cpp:40-107,128-183` uses one reserved base, a separately mapped base extent, and per-layer extra extents. Slot IDs 0..143 remain three per layer; extra IDs follow in a disjoint range and `slot_layer()`/membership resolve them explicitly. Capacity offsets are fixed after reservation. Extra payload offsets need not be VMM-granularity aligned because the enclosing physical extents are mapped at their own aligned starts/sizes.
- Fill/publication in `phase_cache_owner.cpp:188-273` only stages a fill after the slot is physically attached and validates full source bytes by readback before publishing the host/device residency table. Failed copy/readback or inconsistent publication poisons the owner. `ExpertCache::device_slot` checks owner backing, so unbacked IDs resolve null.
- Before growth, the caller checks SessionState owner/geometry, no adaptive producers, verifier commit completion, and device sync; then snapshots stats and calls `sp.reset()` before measuring free memory and mapping extras (`generate.cpp:7946-7985`). Growth fills the 16 additional ranked slots per layer, verifies bytes, publishes, and checks full 912-slot membership (`generate.cpp:7982-8012`).
- Before a second GEN, the source invalidates extras and completes the checked residency upload before unmapping; it then reinitializes Prefill using the same SessionState and 8192 chunk before allowing the prompt (`generate.cpp:8014-8035`). Request admission checks fresh `GEN`, `ckpt=0`, `pin=0`, PCIe=0, token bounds and context bounds before `begin_gen` (`generate.cpp:8421-8434,8525-8534`). Unsupported command prefixes are rejected before request dispatch (`generate.cpp:8051-8055`).
- Verifier gets the full-capacity offset table before initialization (`generate.cpp:5947-5963`, `verify.cpp:435-441`); phase guards run before verifier submissions (`verify.cpp:208,1444`). Uniform token graph creation rejects phase/native offset-table caches (`session.cpp:849-850`). In this selected route, the stable virtual base and immutable offset array preserve raw cache aliases across map/unmap cycles.
- Detach failure retains the uncertain physical handle and poisons the owner; failed extra-map rollback drains first and does not retry. Close unmaps extents before freeing the full reservation and only destroys physical handles after successful unmap (`phase_cache_owner.cpp:128-183,275-300`). QUIT quiesces, resets a live Prefill, destroys the phase verifier and session/token graphs, clears raw reader pointers, then closes VMM and frees the device residency table (`generate.cpp:10541-10555`). This is source evidence, not proof that all runtime queues/events are quiescent on target.
- R333's omitted Gemm lazy `tc_w/tc_x` owner is explicitly handled by replacing Prefill's `Impl` in `sp.reset()`; no separate alias-free omission found in the new cycle.

## Delta from prior reports and limits

R322 already identified the serialized retire/grow and invalidate/unmap/reinitialize lifecycle requirement. R333 added Gemm lazy allocations and scratch/session aliases. The v3 implementation report already records the major source wiring and explicitly leaves GPU/runtime/two-GEN behavior unverified. R337 adds the distinct device-vs-context VMM granularity guard gap. It does not replace or weaken any Main qualification step in `MAIN_TEST_PLAN.txt`; in particular, perform no actual phase treatment until Main establishes actual provider granularity values and finishes its source/binary/provider and two-fresh-GEN gates.
